title: Verb ようと思う
shortExplanation: Express intention or plan to do something; 'I think I will', 'I plan to', 'I intend to'.
longExplanation: The ようと思う grammar point is used to express the intention or plan to do something in the future. It can be translated as 'I think I will', 'I plan to', or 'I intend to' in English. The formation involves using the volitional form of the verb followed by と思う.

examples.jp: 明日、映画を見ようと思います。
examples.romaji: Ashita, eiga o miyou to omoimasu.
examples.en: I think I will watch a movie tomorrow.

examples.jp: 週末に友達と遊ぼうと思っています。
examples.romaji: Shuumatsu ni tomodachi to asobou to omotteimasu.
examples.en: I plan to hang out with friends on the weekend.

examples.jp: 勉強をもっと頑張ろうと思う。
examples.romaji: Benkyou o motto ganbarou to omou.

examples.jp: 来年は海外旅行に行こうと思っている。
examples.romaji: Rainen wa kaigai ryokou ni ikou to omotteiru.
examples.en: I plan to go on an overseas trip next year.

usageNote: "I think I will.../I plan to" - a slightly softer statement of intention than つもりだ.
